----

function isAvailableInTimeSlot(
  availability: { startTime: Date; endTime: Date; days: number[] },
  now: dayjs.Dayjs,
  meetingEndTime: dayjs.Dayjs
): boolean {
  const startTime = dayjs(availability.startTime).utc().format("HH:mm");
  const endTime = dayjs(availability.endTime).utc().format("HH:mm");

  const periodStart = now
    .startOf("day")
    .hour(parseInt(startTime.split(":")[0], 10))
    .minute(parseInt(startTime.split(":")[1], 10));
  const periodEnd = now
    .startOf("day")
    .hour(parseInt(endTime.split(":")[0], 10))
    .minute(parseInt(endTime.split(":")[1], 10));

  const isWithinPeriod =
    now.isBetween(periodStart, periodEnd, null, "[)") &&
    meetingEndTime.isBetween(periodStart, periodEnd, null, "(]");

  return isWithinPeriod;
}

export type PublicEventType = Awaited<ReturnType<typeof getPublicEvent>>;

export async function getEventTypeHosts({
  hosts,
  fetchAllUsers = false,
  prisma,
}: {
  hosts: Prisma.EventTypeGetPayload<{ select: ReturnType<typeof getPublicEventSelect> }>["hosts"];
  fetchAllUsers?: boolean;
  prisma: PrismaClient;
}) {
  const usersAsHosts = hosts.map((host) => host.user);

  // Enrich users in a single batch call
  const enrichedUsers = await new UserRepository(prisma).enrichUsersWithTheirProfiles(usersAsHosts);

  // Map enriched users back to the hosts
  const enrichedHosts = hosts.map((host, index) => ({
    ...host,
    user: enrichedUsers[index],
  }));

const eventData = getPublicEventSelect(true);

type Event = Prisma.EventTypeGetPayload<{ select: typeof eventData }>;

type GetProfileFromEventInput = Omit<Event, "hosts"> & {
  hosts?: Event["hosts"];
  subsetOfHosts: Event["hosts"];
};

export function getProfileFromEvent(event: GetProfileFromEventInput) {
  const { team, subsetOfHosts: hosts, owner } = event;
  const nonTeamProfile = hosts?.[0]?.user || owner;
  const profile = team || nonTeamProfile;
  if (!profile) throw new Error("Event has no owner");

  const styleProfile = team || event.parent?.team || nonTeamProfile;
  const username = "username" in profile ? profile.username : team?.slug;
  const weekStart = hosts?.[0]?.user?.weekStart || owner?.weekStart || "Monday";
  const eventMetaData = eventTypeMetaDataSchemaWithTypedApps.parse(event.metadata || {});
  const userMetaData = userMetadataSchema.parse(profile.metadata || {});

  return {
    username,
    name: profile.name,
    weekStart,
    image: team
      ? getOrgOrTeamAvatar(team)
      : getUserAvatarUrl({
          avatarUrl: nonTeamProfile?.avatarUrl,
        }),
    brandColor: styleProfile.brandColor,
    darkBrandColor: styleProfile.darkBrandColor,
    theme: styleProfile.theme,
    bookerLayouts: bookerLayoutsSchema.parse(
      eventMetaData?.bookerLayouts ||
        (userMetaData && "defaultBookerLayouts" in userMetaData ? userMetaData.defaultBookerLayouts : null)
    ),
  };
}

export async function getUsersFromEvent(
  event: Omit<Event, "owner" | "hosts"> & {
    owner:
      | (Event["owner"] & {
          profile: UserProfile;
        })
      | null;
    hosts?: (Omit<Event["hosts"][number], "user"> & {
      user: Event["hosts"][number]["user"] & {
        profile: UserProfile;
      };
    })[];
    subsetOfHosts: (Omit<Event["hosts"][number], "user"> & {
      user: Event["hosts"][number]["user"] & {
        profile: UserProfile;
      };
    })[];
  },
  prisma: PrismaClient
) {
  const { team, hosts, subsetOfHosts, owner, id } = event;
  if (team) {
    const eventHosts = hosts?.length ? hosts : subsetOfHosts;
    // getOwnerFromUsersArray is used here for backward compatibility when team event type has users[] but not hosts[]
    return eventHosts.length
      ? eventHosts.filter((host) => host.user.username).map(mapHostsToUsers)
      : ((await getOwnerFromUsersArray(prisma, id)) ?? []);
  }
  if (!owner) {
    return null;
  }
  const { username, name, weekStart, profile, avatarUrl } = owner;
  const organizationId = profile?.organization?.id ?? null;
  return [
    {
      username,
      name,
      weekStart,
      organizationId,
      avatarUrl,
      profile,
      bookerUrl: getBookerBaseUrlSync(owner.profile?.organization?.slug ?? null),
    },
  ];
}

async function getOwnerFromUsersArray(prisma: PrismaClient, eventTypeId: number) {
  const { users } = await prisma.eventType.findUniqueOrThrow({
    where: { id: eventTypeId },
    select: {
      users: {
        select: {
          avatarUrl: true,
          username: true,
          name: true,
          weekStart: true,
          id: true,
        },
      },
    },
  });
  if (!users.length) return null;

  // Batch enrich users in a single call
  const enrichedUsers = await new UserRepository(prisma).enrichUsersWithTheirProfiles(users);

  // Map the enriched users back to include the organization info
  const usersWithUserProfile = enrichedUsers.map((user) => ({
    ...user,
    organizationId: user.profile?.organization?.id ?? null,
    organization: user.profile?.organization,
    profile: user.profile,
  }));

  return [
    {
      ...usersWithUserProfile[0],
      bookerUrl: getBookerBaseUrlSync(usersWithUserProfile[0].organization?.slug ?? null),
    },
  ];
}

function mapHostsToUsers(host: {
  user: Pick<UserType, "username" | "name" | "weekStart" | "avatarUrl"> & {
    profile: UserProfile;
  };
}) {
  return {
    username: host.user.username,
    name: host.user.name,
    avatarUrl: host.user.avatarUrl,
    weekStart: host.user.weekStart,
    organizationId: host.user.profile?.organizationId ?? null,
    bookerUrl: getBookerBaseUrlSync(host.user.profile?.organization?.slug ?? null),
    profile: host.user.profile,
  };
}

export const processEventDataShared = async ({
  eventData,
  metadata,
  prisma,
}: {
  eventData: Prisma.EventTypeGetPayload<{ select: ReturnType<typeof getPublicEventSelect> }>;
  metadata: ReturnType<typeof eventTypeMetaDataSchemaWithTypedApps.parse>;
  prisma: PrismaClient;
}) => {
  let showInstantEventConnectNowModal = eventData.isInstantEvent ?? false;
  if (eventData.isInstantEvent && eventData.instantMeetingSchedule?.id) {
    const { id, timeZone } = eventData.instantMeetingSchedule;
    showInstantEventConnectNowModal = await isCurrentlyAvailable({
      prisma,
      instantMeetingScheduleId: id,
      availabilityTimezone: timeZone ?? "Europe/London",
      length: eventData.length,
    });
  }

  return {
    ...eventData,
    bookerLayouts: bookerLayoutsSchema.parse(metadata?.bookerLayouts || null),
    description: markdownToSafeHTML(eventData.description),
    metadata,
    customInputs: customInputSchema.array().parse(eventData.customInputs || []),
    locations: privacyFilteredLocations((eventData.locations || []) as LocationObject[]),
    bookingFields: getBookingFieldsWithSystemFields(eventData),
    recurringEvent: isRecurringEvent(eventData.recurringEvent)
      ? parseRecurringEvent(eventData.recurringEvent)
      : null,
    isDynamic: false,
    showInstantEventConnectNowModal,
  };
};

```typescript
import { eventTypeColor } from "@calcom/prisma/zod-utils";

export type BookingPageColors = {
  backgroundColor?: string;
  textColor?: string;
};

export function getBookingPageColors(storedColors: unknown): BookingPageColors | null {
  const parsed = eventTypeColor.safeParse(storedColors);
  // One malformed row must never break a booking page, so it falls back to the theme colors.
  if (!parsed.success || !parsed.data) return null;

  const { backgroundColor, textColor } = parsed.data;
  if (!backgroundColor && !textColor) return null;

  return {
    ...(backgroundColor ? { backgroundColor } : {}),
    ...(textColor ? { textColor } : {}),
  };
}

// The stored value also holds the accent colors, which the editor promises are never shown to
// bookers, so the public payload carries only the booking page colors.
export function withBookingPageColors<T extends { eventTypeColor: unknown }>(event: T) {
  const { eventTypeColor: storedColors, ...eventWithoutStoredColors } = event;
  return {
    ...eventWithoutStoredColors,
    bookingPageColors: getBookingPageColors(storedColors),
  };
}

```

```typescript
import type { BookingPageColors } from "@calcom/features/eventtypes/lib/getBookingPageColors";
import type { CSSProperties } from "react";

// An inline style renders on the server, so the page never flashes the theme colors, and the
// values stay inside this booker during client navigation to another event.
export function getBookingPageColorStyle(colors: BookingPageColors | null | undefined): CSSProperties {
  if (!colors) return {};

  const { backgroundColor, textColor } = colors;
  // The booker container paints from --cal-bg-muted in dark mode, so both must be set.
  const backgroundVariables = backgroundColor
    ? { "--cal-bg": backgroundColor, "--cal-bg-muted": backgroundColor }
    : {};
  // Mixing with transparent keeps the secondary text readable over any background color.
  const secondaryTextColor = textColor ? `color-mix(in srgb, ${textColor} 70%, transparent)` : undefined;
  const textVariables = textColor
    ? {
        "--cal-text": textColor,
        "--cal-text-emphasis": textColor,
        "--cal-text-subtle": secondaryTextColor,
        "--cal-text-muted": secondaryTextColor,
      }
    : {};

  return { ...backgroundVariables, ...textVariables } as CSSProperties;
}

```

import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

import { getBookingPageColors, withBookingPageColors } from "./getBookingPageColors";

const accentColors = { lightEventTypeColor: "#292929", darkEventTypeColor: "#fafafa" };

describe("getBookingPageColors", () => {
  it("returns null when the editor toggle is off", () => {
    expect(getBookingPageColors(null)).toBeNull();
  });

  it("returns null when the stored value is malformed", () => {
    expect(getBookingPageColors({ lightEventTypeColor: 3 })).toBeNull();
    expect(getBookingPageColors({ ...accentColors, backgroundColor: "red" })).toBeNull();
    expect(getBookingPageColors("not an object")).toBeNull();
  });

  it("returns null when only the accent colors are stored", () => {
    expect(getBookingPageColors(accentColors)).toBeNull();
  });

  it("returns only the background color when the text color is missing", () => {
    expect(getBookingPageColors({ ...accentColors, backgroundColor: "#101010" })).toEqual({
      backgroundColor: "#101010",
    });
  });

  it("returns only the text color when the background color is missing", () => {
    expect(getBookingPageColors({ ...accentColors, textColor: "#ffffff" })).toEqual({
      textColor: "#ffffff",
    });
  });

  it("returns both colors and no accent colors", () => {
    expect(
      getBookingPageColors({ ...accentColors, backgroundColor: "#101010", textColor: "#ffffff" })
    ).toEqual({ backgroundColor: "#101010", textColor: "#ffffff" });
  });
});

describe("withBookingPageColors", () => {
  it("replaces the stored colors with the booking page colors", () => {
    const result = withBookingPageColors({
      id: 1,
      eventTypeColor: { ...accentColors, backgroundColor: "#101010", textColor: "#ffffff" },
    });

    expect(result).toEqual({
      id: 1,
      bookingPageColors: { backgroundColor: "#101010", textColor: "#ffffff" },
    });
    expect(result).not.toHaveProperty("eventTypeColor");
  });

  it("sets null booking page colors when the toggle is off", () => {
    expect(withBookingPageColors({ id: 1, eventTypeColor: null })).toEqual({
      id: 1,
      bookingPageColors: null,
    });
  });
});

```

# /passoff

**The single highest-leverage artifact there is.** The next agent will not see this
conversation, this reasoning, or this context. A prompt that assumes any of it produces a
session that rediscovers what you already knew.

Nine parts, in this order. Skip one only when it is genuinely empty, and say so.

1. **Title.** Imperative, naming the change, not the area. *"Drag the week grid: windows edited
   where they are drawn"*, not *"week grid work"*.
2. **The header line.** `**Model: <tier>. Lane <X>. Waits on <what>.**` Plus the worktree
   instruction when the item needs its own. Pick the tier by asking four questions in order and
   taking the tier of the first yes: does the prompt state the change and the place (Light,
   where configured); does it have to place a clear change (Mechanical); does it have to find a
   cause or choose a design (Default); could a wrong answer pass every gate and a person's test
   (Deep). When two tiers fit, take the lower and name the gate or picture that catches a wrong
   answer; if none does, take the higher. After a failed build, escalation goes up one tier and
   never down. **Important:** Never assign a model tier above the
   repo's tier ceiling (if it has one). Check the repo's `CLAUDE.md` for its ceiling before
   writing a pass-off for it.
3. **Orientation.** Who they are picking up, what to read first and in what order, and the
   session rules restated **inline**, not by reference. A prompt is pasted alone, and a rule
   one file away is a rule that does not arrive.
4. **Why this exists**, in product terms. This is what lets the next agent make a hundred small
   judgment calls the prompt does not cover.
5. **What is fixed.** *"Read these before changing anything; do not relitigate them."* The
   verified facts with citations, the invariants, the house precedent to copy in place of a new
   invention, the constraint that makes this smaller than it looks. This section is where this
   session's reading is **banked** instead of re-paid.
6. **Do these, in order.** Numbered, each carrying its reason and its constraint. A step that
   says only what to do gets done differently than intended.
7. **Ask before building.** The named decisions that are the owner's, each with what makes it a
   real question. Say explicitly that both are their calls, and that either answer may be no.
   Where a question must wait for the owner even in an unattended run, write **owner's call**
   before it: `/autopilot`'s decider holds a row on those words and never answers it.
8. **Not in scope, whoever asks.** The negative list, named. It survives a persuasive
   mid-session argument in a way that an unstated boundary does not.
9. **Hand back.** The literal gate commands that must be green, what the owner should do and
   see, and the commit step.

`personal-config passoff next` prints the next `OPEN` item with its prompt and its model line,
and warns when something already in flight owns one of the same files; `personal-config passoff
claim <n>` marks the row `IN FLIGHT` and dates it. Neither writes the prompt: that is this
skill's work.

**Where it goes.** One file per item, `passoff/<n>-<slug>.md`, and its row in the table, in
the same edit. The file opens with `# <n>. <Title>`, then the dated line saying why it exists,
then the nine parts. `personal-config passoff next` reports the next free number, read from the
table, the folder and the archive: a number is never reused, even after its row has left the
table. The slug is the title in lower case, each run of other characters one hyphen, cut at a
hyphen to at most 48 characters. It is named once and never renamed.
On a 1.x board, with no `passoff/` folder beside it, the prompt is a `### <n>.` section below the table.

**A prompt rots the moment it is executed.** The item's close-out section is the truth; the prompt is the
ask. Never paste a prompt marked done: a fresh session would build it again.

# Draft issue: partial-day out-of-office badge and redirect

Drafted 2026-10-18 for `zach-short`. Not posted. Private, untracked.

## How to post (for Zach, after review)

- Title: `Show the away badge and redirect for partial-day out-of-office entries`
- Labels to propose: `enhancement`, `effort:medium`. Both exist (`gh label list -R CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy`, read 2026-10-18). The template adds `✨ feature` and `🚨 needs approval` on its own, if those labels exist on this fork. Neither is in the label list, so check what GitHub actually applies.
- Template: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.md`. The body below keeps its headings and adds the sections issue #6 used (User Story, User Scenario, Acceptance Criteria, Out of Scope, Open Questions, Technical Notes), so it reads like #6.
- Milestone: Sprint 2, once PASSOFF item 23 creates it.
- The template ends with a "House rules" footer. This draft leaves it out because its wording breaks the writing rules for this file. When you post through the GitHub form, the form fills that footer in. Keep it there. For the same reason one heading reads "you would like" here. Keep the form's own heading text.
- Duplicate check: `gh issue list -R CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy --state all --search "out of office partial"` returns only #6 (closed by PR #85).
- Code citations are from `origin/main` at `cc65a9670f` (2026-10-12). The local branch `short` does not contain PR #85, so its line numbers differ. Check the citations again on the branch you cut for this issue.

Everything below the line is the issue body.

---

### Is your proposal related to a problem?

PR #85 (closes #6) lets a host set a leave time and a return time on an out-of-office entry. The booking page now removes the slots inside that window, but it does that the way it removes a calendar event: the slots are gone, and nothing says why. A whole-day entry shows the "away" panel with the reason, the emoji, the public note and, when a redirect user is set, a "Book with <name>" button. A partial-day entry shows none of these. PR #85 names this as a known limit ("Partial-day entries do not show the "away" badge or a redirect on the booking page") and describes "alternative 1" as the path to fix it.

### Describe the solution you would like

Build alternative 1 from PR #85: teach the per-day out-of-office map about time ranges. Slots inside a partial-day window stay in the slot list, marked `away` with the entry's reason, emoji, note and redirect user, the same data a whole-day entry carries. The booker then renders one "away" panel at the place in the day where the window falls, between the slots before it and the slots after it. Away slots stay unbookable, as they are for whole days today.

### User Story

As an attendee who opens a host's booking page, I want to see that the host is away for part of the day, and book with their redirect user if one is set, so that I know why some times are missing and where to book instead.

### User Scenario

A host works 09:00 to 17:00 and has a partial-day entry from 14:00 to 16:00 with the reason "Doctor" and a public note. An attendee opens the booking page for that day. Slots from 09:00 run up to the slot that ends at 14:00. Below them is the away panel with the emoji, the reason and the note. Below the panel, slots resume at 16:00. If the entry has a redirect user, the panel also shows "Book with <name>", and the button opens that user's booking page on the same date.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. For a partial-day entry, every slot that overlaps the window is returned with `away: true` and the entry's `fromUser`, `toUser`, `reason`, `emoji`, and the note when `showNotePublicly` is on. Slots that do not overlap the window have no `away` flag.
2. A slot marked away for a partial-day entry cannot be booked. Booking it returns the same error as booking inside a whole-day entry.
3. On the booking page, a day with a partial-day window shows the bookable slots before the window, one away panel, and the bookable slots after the window, in that order. This holds when the window is at the start of the day, in the middle, or at the end.
4. When the entry has a redirect user, the away panel shows "Book with <name>", and clicking it opens that user's booking page on the same date, as it does for a whole-day entry.
5. A partial-day entry that covers all of the host's working hours on a day renders that day exactly as a whole-day entry does, in the time list and in the date picker.
6. Whole-day entries, holidays and calendar busy times render and block exactly as before. Existing tests for them pass unchanged.
7. API v2 slot responses do not change. Away slots stay filtered out of them (`slots-output.service.ts:49` and `:119` already do this).
8. Unit tests cover criteria 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6, including a window on a DST change day in America/New_York.

### Out of Scope

- Setting a redirect user from the out-of-office form. The redirect switch is disabled in this fork (`hasTeamPlan = false`, `CreateOrEditOutOfOfficeModal.tsx:190`, used at `:483`). This issue only renders a redirect that is already stored.
- Partial-day entries through API v2, which still stores whole days (PR #85, Known limits).
- Team and round-robin events. Their availability uses `oooExcludedDateRanges` (`getAggregatedAvailability.ts:43` and `:65`), so whole-day entries show no away panel there either.
- Changes to the out-of-office form or list from PR #85.

### Open Questions

- Which slots count as "inside" the window? A 30-minute event at 13:45 overlaps a 14:00 leave time. Criterion 1 says any overlap marks the slot away. The other option is to drop overlapping slots and mark only the slots fully inside the window. A window shorter than one slot interval (for example 14:10 to 14:20) may otherwise produce no away slot and so no panel.
- What does the panel say for a 2-hour entry? Today it says the host is away with no times. Should a partial-day panel show the leave and return times ("Away 2:00 PM to 4:00 PM")? That needs a new string in `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json` and the times in the attendee's timezone, not the host's.
- Two partial-day entries on one day (for example 10:00 to 11:00 and 14:00 to 15:00): two panels, or one? The per-day map holds one entry per date today, so this decides the shape of the data.
- Timezone edges. The map is keyed by the host's date (`slots.ts:189-192` formats the slot in `datesOutOfOfficeTimeZone`). An attendee several hours away can see a host's evening window on their next day. Is it enough that the panel sits between the right slots in the attendee's view, or must the panel also say the host's local times?
- The redirect cannot be set from the UI or from API v2 in this fork today. Is criterion 4 worth keeping if it can be shown only with a unit test and a hand-edited `OutOfOfficeEntry.toUserId` row?

### Technical Notes (from reading the code, to be confirmed while implementing)

Line numbers are from `origin/main` at `cc65a9670f`.

- **Where partial entries leave the map today.** `UserAvailabilityService.calculateOutOfOfficeRanges` returns early for any entry that fails `isWholeDayOutOfOffice` (`packages/features/availability/lib/getUserAvailability.ts:748`). The predicate is at `packages/features/schedules/lib/date-ranges.ts:228`. The partial entries go to `getPartialDayOutOfOfficeRanges` instead (`date-ranges.ts:248`, called at `getUserAvailability.ts:482`).
- **Why the slots vanish.** The partial ranges are appended to the busy times (`getUserAvailability.ts:651-657`) and subtracted from both `dateRanges` and `oooExcludedDateRanges` (`:659-660`). A whole-day entry is different: it stays in `dateRanges`, so its slots are generated and then marked away, and it is removed only from `oooExcludedDateRanges` through `groupedOOO` (`date-ranges.ts:297-300` and `:354-361`). To get away slots, a partial window must follow the same split: subtract it from `oooExcludedDateRanges` only, and keep it in `dateRanges`.
- **Booking stays blocked.** `ensureAvailableUsers` checks a booking against `oooExcludedDateRanges` (`packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking/ensureAvailableUsers.ts:220`), so once the window is removed there, a booking inside it is still rejected. Criterion 2 needs a test for this.
- **Slot marking is date-level.** `buildSlotsWithDateRanges` looks up `datesOutOfOffice[YYYY-MM-DD]` and marks every slot on that date (`packages/features/schedules/lib/slots.ts:187-221`). It needs a time check for partial entries. `IOutOfOfficeData` (`getUserAvailability.ts:209`) maps a date to one entry, so the type must carry the window (for example optional `start` and `end`, or a list per date). See the open question on two entries in one day.
- **The booker assumes away means a whole day.** `AvailableTimes` shows the panel when every slot is away, or when only the first or only the last slot is away, and it hides every away slot (`apps/web/modules/bookings/components/AvailableTimes.tsx:266-293`). A mid-day window has neither its first nor its last slot away, so no panel renders. It must render the panel at the first away slot of each run. `AvailableTimeSlots` decides that a day is away from its first slot only (`apps/web/modules/bookings/components/AvailableTimeSlots.tsx:206`, comment "since OOO is date-level"), which hides the time-format toggle when a window starts the day.
- **The redirect.** The "Book with" button is in `OutOfOfficeInSlots.tsx`, which calls `router.push` to `/${toUser.username}` with the date. It already works from the slot data, so criterion 4 needs only the data in criterion 1.
- **Other readers of `away`.** `DatePicker.tsx:256-269` marks a day as away only when every slot is away, which gives criterion 5 for free. `useNonEmptyScheduleDays.ts:13` and the weekly view `Empty.tsx:66` also read the flag. Check that they do not change for a partial window.
- **Test that must change.** PR #85 added `getUserAvailability.outOfOffice.timezone.test.ts`, which asserts that a partial-day entry "stays off the away map". This issue reverses that on purpose. Update the case, do not delete it.
- **DST.** Keep the `wallClockToTimeZone` parse from PR #85 (`date-ranges.ts:241-246`) for the window edges. `.tz(zone, true)` returns the wrong offset near a DST change.

### Additional context

Estimate: medium (`effort:medium`). The likely files are `getUserAvailability.ts`, `date-ranges.ts`, `slots.ts`, `AvailableTimes.tsx`, `AvailableTimeSlots.tsx`, plus `slots.test.ts`, `date-ranges.test.ts`, `getUserAvailability.outOfOffice.timezone.test.ts`, and a new test for `AvailableTimes`. That is about 5 code files and 4 test files, under the 10-file limit in `AGENTS.md`. The slot engine part reuses a pattern that whole-day entries already use, which keeps it medium. The booker change is the part that could grow, because no unit test covers `AvailableTimes` today (`apps/web/modules/bookings/components/` has tests only for `Booker`, `BookingDetailsSheet` and `DatePicker`). If the diff passes 500 lines, split it: engine and slots first, booker second.

### Requirement/Document

### Is your proposal related to a problem?

<!--
  Provide a clear and concise description of what the problem is.
  For example, "I'm always frustrated when..."
-->

As a user, I want to have the ability to set my event to have a specific background and foreground color. It would also be nice to have the ability to set a background picture as a substitute for a color as well.

### Describe the solution you'd like

<!--
  Provide a clear and concise description of what you want to happen.
-->
A setting leaflet underneath the layout leaflet that allows for setting a background/foreground color, as well as an image for the given event.



### User Story

As an event host, I want to set a background color and a text color for an event type's public booking page, so that each event looks the way I want when attendees book it.

### User Scenario

A host runs two events, "Design review" and "Coffee chat". For "Coffee chat" the host opens the event type, finds the new color setting under the layout setting, picks a warm background and a dark text color, and saves. The booking link for "Coffee chat" now shows those colors. "Design review" looks the same as before.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. The event type editor has a background color setting and a text color setting under the layout setting. It is off by default.
2. When the setting is off or has never been set, the booking page looks exactly as it does today.
3. When colors are set, the public booking page for that event type shows the chosen background and text colors.
4. The colors apply to one event type only. Other event types of the same host are unchanged.
5. After saving and reloading the editor, the pickers show the saved values.
6. Only valid color values (hex) are accepted. An invalid value is rejected on save and shows an error.
7. If the text and background colors fail a contrast check, the editor shows a warning.

### Out of Scope

- A background image (named in the original request; deferred so this issue stays on colors).
- Gradients, fonts and other styling.
- Team-level or account-level themes.
- Colors in emails and calendar invites.

### Open Questions

- Does "event" mean the public booking page (assumed here) or the host's own dashboard views?
- One color pair, or separate light and dark theme values like the existing event type color?
- If the booking page's own light or dark theme conflicts with the chosen colors, which one wins?
- Should failing the contrast check only warn (assumed here), or block saving?
- Where do the values live: new columns, or the existing JSON? New columns need approval first, because the repo rules ask before schema changes.

### Technical Notes (from reading the code, to be confirmed while implementing)

- `EventType.eventTypeColor` already stores a light and a dark color (`packages/prisma/zod-utils.ts`) and has an "Event type color" toggle in the Advanced tab (`apps/web/modules/event-types/components/tabs/advanced/EventAdvancedTab.tsx`). It only draws an accent stripe in the event types list, the bookings list and the bookings calendar view. It is not applied to the booking page. It is the closest existing pattern (storage, toggle, contrast warning text in the translations).
- The booking page takes brand colors from the user or team in `packages/features/bookings/Booker/utils/use-brand-colors.tsx`, a likely place to start for applying per-event colors.
- The planning doc scored this 4 points and assumed a schema change. The GitHub label says `effort:high`, which fits only if the image is included.

---
title: Never Introduce Breaking API Changes
impact: CRITICAL
impactDescription: Maintains developer trust and prevents integration nightmares
tags: api, stability, versioning, backwards-compatibility
---

## Never Introduce Breaking API Changes

**Impact: CRITICAL**

Once an API endpoint is public, it must remain stable. Breaking changes destroy developer trust and create integration nightmares for our users.

**Strategies for avoiding breaking changes:**
- Always add new fields as optional
- Use API versioning when you must change existing behavior
- Deprecate old endpoints gracefully with clear migration paths
- Maintain backward compatibility for at least two major versions

**Incorrect (breaking change):**

```typescript
// v1 - Original response
interface BookingResponse {
  id: number;
  startTime: string; // ISO string
}

// v1 - Breaking change: renamed field
interface BookingResponse {
  id: number;
  start: string; // Renamed from startTime - BREAKS CLIENTS
}
```

**Correct (non-breaking evolution):**

```typescript
// v1 - Original response
interface BookingResponse {
  id: number;
  startTime: string;
}

// v1 - Non-breaking: add new field, keep old one
interface BookingResponse {
  id: number;
  startTime: string; // Keep for backwards compatibility
  start: string; // New preferred field
}
```

**When you must make breaking changes:**
- Create a new API version using date-specific versioning in API v2
- Run both versions simultaneously during transition
- Provide automated migration tools when possible
- Give users ample time to migrate (minimum 6 months for public APIs)
- Document exactly what changed and why

Reference: [Cal.diy Engineering Blog](https://cal.com/blog/engineering-in-2026-and-beyond)

  @Get("/:username/:eventSlug/public")
  async getPublicEventType(
    @Param("username") username: string,
    @Param("eventSlug") eventSlug: string,
    @Query() queryParams: GetPublicEventTypeQueryParams_2024_04_15,
    @Headers(X_CAL_CLIENT_ID) clientId?: string
  ): Promise<GetEventTypePublicOutput> {
    try {
      let orgSlug = queryParams.org;

      if (clientId && !orgSlug && username.includes(`-${clientId}`)) {
        const org = await this.organizationsRepository
          .findTeamIdAndSlugFromClientId(clientId)
          .catch(() => null);
        if (org) {
          orgSlug = org.slug;
        }
      }

      const event = await getPublicEvent(
        username.toLowerCase(),
        eventSlug,
        queryParams.isTeamEvent,
        orgSlug ?? null,
        this.prismaReadService.prisma as unknown as PrismaClient,
        // We should be fine allowing unpublished orgs events to be servable through platform because Platform access is behind license
        // If there is ever a need to restrict this, we can introduce a new query param `fromRedirectOfNonOrgLink`
        true
      );

      return {
        data: event as unknown as PublicEventTypeOutput,
        status: SUCCESS_STATUS,
      };
    } catch (err) {
      if (err instanceof Error) {
        throw new NotFoundException(err.message);
      }
    }
    throw new InternalServerErrorException("Could not find public event.");

    @Param("eventSlug") eventSlug: string,
    @Query() queryParams: GetAtomPublicEventTypeQueryParams
  ): Promise<ApiResponse<PublicEventType>> {
    const { username, teamId, orgId, isTeamEvent } = queryParams;

    const event = await this.eventTypesService.getPublicEventTypeForAtoms({
      username,
      eventSlug,
      isTeamEvent: isTeamEvent ?? false,
      teamId,
      orgId,
    });

    return {
      data: event,
      status: SUCCESS_STATUS,
    };
  }

  async getPublicEventTypeForAtoms({
    username,
    eventSlug,
    isTeamEvent,
    orgId,
    teamId,
  }: {
    username?: string;
    eventSlug: string;
    isTeamEvent?: boolean;
    orgId?: number;
    teamId?: number;
  }): Promise<PublicEventType> {
    const orgSlug = orgId ? await this.getTeamSlug(orgId) : null;

    let usernameOrTeamSlug: string | null = null;
    if (isTeamEvent) {
      if (!teamId) {
        throw new BadRequestException("teamId is required for team events, please provide a valid teamId");
      }
      usernameOrTeamSlug = await this.getTeamSlug(teamId);
    } else {
      if (!username) {
        throw new BadRequestException(
          "username is required for non-team events, please provide a valid username"
        );
      }
      usernameOrTeamSlug = username;
    }

    usernameOrTeamSlug = usernameOrTeamSlug.toLowerCase();

    try {
      let event = await getPublicEvent(
        usernameOrTeamSlug,
        eventSlug,
        isTeamEvent,
        orgSlug,
        this.dbRead.prisma as unknown as PrismaClient,
        true
      );

      const usernamePossiblyNotFromProfile = username && orgId && !event;
      if (usernamePossiblyNotFromProfile) {
        const user = await this.usersRepository.findByUsernameWithProfile(username);
        if (user) {
          const profile = await this.usersService.getUserMainProfile(user);
          if (profile?.username) {
            event = await getPublicEvent(
              profile.username,
              eventSlug,
              isTeamEvent,
              orgSlug,
              this.dbRead.prisma as unknown as PrismaClient,
              true
            );
          }
        }
      }

      if (!event) {
        throw new NotFoundException(`Event type with slug ${eventSlug} not found`);
      }

      return event;

## 0.0.51
Released to support PR https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy/pull/17224 which enabled attendee specified location during booking.

## 0.0.41
Released to support handle cancel booking passing oauth client id to webhooks.

## 0.0.38
#### Feature: Added Support for AdvancedTab Event-Type Attributes in API
- **Booker Layouts**: 
  - Added `transformBookerLayoutsApiToInternal` translator to enable the `bookerLayouts` attribute in the event-type API.
  - Added `transformBookerLayoutsInternalToApi` translator to improve clarity and readability of `bookerLayouts` response data.

- **Event-Type Colors**:
  - Added `transformEventColorsApiToInternal` translator to enable the `color` attribute in the event-type API.
  - Added `transformEventTypeColorsInternalToApi` translator to enhance the readability of the `color` attribute in the response.

- **Confirmation Policy**:
  - Added `transformConfirmationPolicyApiToInternal` translator to enable the `confirmationPolicy` attribute in the event-type API.
  - Added `transformRequiresConfirmationInternalToApi` translator to improve the readability of `requiresConfirmation` data in the response.

- **Seats**:
  - Added `transformSeatsApiToInternal` translator to enable the `seats` attribute in the event-type API.
  - Added `transformSeatsInternalToApi` translator to enhance readability and clarity of the `seats` data.

## 0.0.37
Released to support PR https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy/pull/16200

## 0.0.36

Released to support PR https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy/pull/16685

import { eventTypeColor } from "@calcom/prisma/zod-utils";

export type BookingPageColors = {
  backgroundColor?: string;
  textColor?: string;
};

export function getBookingPageColors(storedColors: unknown): BookingPageColors | null {
  const parsed = eventTypeColor.safeParse(storedColors);
  // One malformed row must never break a booking page, so it falls back to the theme colors.
  if (!parsed.success || !parsed.data) return null;

  const { backgroundColor, textColor } = parsed.data;
  if (!backgroundColor && !textColor) return null;

  return {
    ...(backgroundColor ? { backgroundColor } : {}),
    ...(textColor ? { textColor } : {}),
  };
}

// The stored value also holds the accent colors, which the editor promises are never shown to
// bookers, so the public payload carries only the booking page colors.
export function withBookingPageColors<T extends { eventTypeColor: unknown }>(event: T) {
  const { eventTypeColor: storedColors, ...eventWithoutStoredColors } = event;
  return {
    ...eventWithoutStoredColors,
    bookingPageColors: getBookingPageColors(storedColors),
  };
}

import { eventTypeColor as eventTypeColorSchema } from "@calcom/prisma/zod-utils";

type EventTypeColor = z.infer<typeof eventTypeColorSchema>;
export function isEventTypeColor(obj: unknown): obj is EventTypeColor {

}

**Why this exists.** A host can now give one event type a booking page background and text color in
the web editor. API v2 clients cannot read or set them, and worse, an API v2 update that sends the
existing `color` object wipes them out. A client that reads an event type and writes it back loses
the host's colors without any error. After this step, API v2 keeps the colors it does not touch and
can read and write them. Every existing API v2 request must keep working unchanged.

**What is fixed. Read these before you change anything, and do not reopen them.**

1. **Storage.** One JSON column, `EventType.eventTypeColor`:
   `{ lightEventTypeColor, darkEventTypeColor, backgroundColor?, textColor? } | null`
   (`packages/prisma/zod-utils.ts:263-271`). `backgroundColor` and `textColor` must match
   `/^#([0-9A-Fa-f]{3}){1,2}$/` (`hexColor`, `:261`). No schema change and no migration.
2. **Only API version 2024_06_14 has colors.** The input class is `EventTypeColor_2024_06_14`
   (`packages/platform/types/event-types/event-types_2024_06_14/inputs/event-type-color.input.ts:5-21`),
   with required `lightThemeHex` and `darkThemeHex`, each `@IsHexColor() @IsString()`. The internal
   type `EventTypeColorsTransformedSchema` (`:23-26`) has only the two accent colors. The optional
   `color` field sits on the create base class (`create-event-type.input.ts:444-445`) and the update
   base class (`update-event-type.input.ts:384-385`), so user and team event types share it. The
   output reuses the same class (`outputs/event-type.output.ts:402-404`).
3. **Both transformers drop the new fields.** API to DB:
   `transformEventColorsApiToInternal`
   (`apps/api/v2/src/platform/event-types/event-types_2024_06_14/transformers/api-to-internal/event-colors.ts:6-15`),
   called through `transformInputEventTypeColor` (`services/input-event-types.service.ts:426-428`) at
   `:180` (create) and `:291` (update). DB to API: `transformEventTypeColorsInternalToApi`
   (`transformers/internal-to-api/event-type-colors.ts:3-10`), called from `transformEventTypeColor`
   (`services/output-event-types.service.ts:420-424`), which parses with `parseEventTypeColor`
   (`packages/lib/isEventTypeColor.ts`). The parse already keeps the new fields.
4. **Why an update wipes the colors.** API v2 updates call the tRPC update handler
   (`packages/platform/libraries/event-types.ts:8`, used at `services/event-types.service.ts:308`),
   which writes the whole JSON value (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/eventTypes/heavy/update.handler.ts:229`).
   So `color: { lightThemeHex, darkThemeHex }` replaces the row's JSON and the booking page colors are
   gone. An update without `color` passes `undefined` and leaves the column alone.

   `forbidNonWhitelisted` (`apps/api/v2/src/bootstrap.ts:59-60`). A client sending `backgroundColor`

   (`node_modules/validator/lib/isHexColor.js:9`). The stored schema does not. A value that passes

   color object, accent colors included, disappears from every reader. The new fields must use the
   stored rule, for example `@Matches` with the same pattern. Grep for a `@Matches(` with a regex in
